title: Shader Alchemy Pool Lab
description: A mystical pool scene where the user dips translucent teacups and animated test objects into enchanted water, mixing custom shader effects. Each object acts as a reagent that alters the pool's fragment shader uniforms—color channels, wave frequency, refraction index, and caustic intensity—with a conservation law ensuring total shader energy remains constant. Users can undo/redo dip sequences to explore different visual combinations.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load pool.glb centered at origin as the base water basin. Load DiffuseTransmissionTeacup.glb and InterpolationTest.glb floating above the pool at different positions. Apply a custom ShaderMaterial to the pool's water mesh using vertex and fragment shaders: the vertex shader should displace vertices with a sine-based wave function controlled by uniform uWaveFreq (default 2.0) and uWaveAmp (default 0.05). The fragment shader should blend a base blue color with uniforms uTintR, uTintG, uTintB (all default 0.0), uRefractionIndex (default 1.33), and uCausticIntensity (default 0.3). Implement a conservation law: the sum uTintR + uTintG + uTintB + uCausticIntensity + uWaveFreq_normalized must always equal 1.0, so increasing one parameter automatically decreases others proportionally. The teacup is the warm reagent: clicking it then clicking the pool performs a dip that increases uTintR by 0.08 and uCausticIntensity by 0.05, with others rebalanced. The InterpolationTest object is the cool reagent: dipping it increases uTintB by 0.1 and uWaveFreq by 0.5, rebalancing others. Add a slider panel with 5 sliders showing all shader uniforms in real-time, each slider also manually adjustable with automatic conservation rebalancing. Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y that restores the entire uniform state stack. Each dip animates the object downward into the pool and back up over 1 second using TWEEN or requestAnimationFrame lerp. Add a reset button. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 5) looking at origin, directional light from (5, 10, 5), ambient light intensity 0.4. Display a step counter and current energy sum. Minimum 10 interaction steps to explore all combinations: 4 teacup dips, 3 interpolation dips, 2 slider adjustments, 1 undo, achieving a target shader state shown as a color swatch in the corner.
